text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, and its symptoms often develop slowly and go unnoticed for months or years. You can review detailed information and support resources via the Pulmonary Hypertension Association or the American Lung Association.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Usually starts during exercise or climbing stairs, and eventually happens even at rest.
Fatigue: Feeling very tired or lacking energy during normal daily tasks.
Dizziness or fainting: Lightheadedness that can happen during physical activity.
Chest pain: Pressure or discomfort in the front of the chest due to heart strain.
Heart palpitations: A racing, pounding, or irregular heartbeat.
Swelling (edema): Fluid buildup causing swollen ankles, legs, or belly area.
Bluish skin or lips: Cyanosis, or a gray/blue tone on the lips, skin, or fingers.
